entry.title: Local AI on Fedora — Obsidian Online (Google AI Studio)

link.title: Local AI on Fedora — Obsidian Online (Google AI Studio)

entry.content:
This is the online half of the pair. The offline post runs a model on the machine. This one sends the same clipped note to Google and gets a short vault note back. The vault, the clipper, and the prompt stay. Ollama does not.

Use this when the laptop cannot keep a 7B model in RAM, or when the local answer keeps turning into a tutorial. The trade is simple: the text of the note leaves the house.

Do not send confidential or secret material — medical notes, passwords, unpublished work, anything you would not paste into a cloud form. That stays on the offline path.

 

What you sign up for

A Google account is enough. Open Google AI Studio and accept the terms. AI Studio then creates a default project and a key.

That key is for the Gemini API. It is not the login of gemini.google.com, and it is not a Gemini Advanced subscription. The chat site and the API are different doors.

New keys created in AI Studio are authorization keys. Copy one from the API keys page. The free tier is enough to tidy notes. Billing is only for higher limits and some larger models. Do not enable it unless a request actually fails for quota.

Never paste the key into a note, a screenshot, or this site. If it leaks, delete it on that page and create another.

 

What does not change

Firefox, Obsidian Web Clipper, and legacy mode are the same as in the offline post. A long Grok or Gemini thread still has to be scrolled and copied in pieces. The API does not see the browser.

Ctrl+P still runs the generator on the open note. The instruction still goes after the pasted dialogue.

 

Point Text Generator at Google

In Obsidian: Settings → Text Generator → provider Google / Gemini (the label depends on the plugin version).

  • API key: paste the key from AI Studio. The field is the only place it belongs.
  • Model: the dropdown is stale. gemini-2.0-flash and gemini-2.5-flash return 404 on a new key. Click the pencil beside the model name and type gemini-3.8-flash (no models/ prefix). If that 404s, try gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Do not trust the names shipped with the plugin. Pro is slower and may want billing.
  • Model: the dropdown is stale. gemini-2.0-flash and gemini-2.5-flash return 404 on a new key. Click the pencil beside the model name and type the current endpoint from the Gemini API models page — today gemini-3.8-flash, with no models/ prefix. If that 404s, try gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Copy the endpoint, not the display name. Do not trust the names shipped with the plugin. Pro is slower and may want billing.
  • Leave the base URL empty unless you run a proxy. The default endpoint is Google’s.

Save, open the clipped note, Ctrl+P, run Text Generator. No Konsole. No localhost.

If the plugin has a system line, use the same clerk instruction as offline:

You are a clerk. You output Markdown. You never explain how to work.

And at the bottom of the note, after the chat:

Turn the dialogue above into a vault note.
Headings: Done / Decisions / Open.
European Portuguese or English — match the dialogue.
No how-to. No jokes. If it is not in the dialogue, omit it.

 

When it fails
  • API key not valid — wrong key, or a key from another Google account. Create it again on the API keys page while logged in as the same user.
  • Model not found — the name in the plugin is stale. Pick Flash from the dropdown, do not type an old gemini-pro id from a 2024 guide.
  • Empty answer — the plugin sent the instruction and not the note. Select the dialogue and generate from the selection.
  • Quota — wait, or shorten the clip. Do not jump to billing for one note.

 

Offline or online
  Offline (Ollama) Online (this post)
Text leaves the PC No Yes
Disk and RAM Model weights None
Speed on a small laptop Slow Fine
Key to protect None AI Studio key
Clipper Same Same

Same vault. Two providers. Pick by the machine, not by the note.
entry.summary: The online pair of the Ollama post. Same Obsidian vault and Firefox clipper, with a Google AI Studio API key instead of a local model.

entry.title: Local AI on Fedora — Ollama and Obsidian Offline

link.title: Local AI on Fedora — Ollama and Obsidian Offline

entry.content:
The point of a local model is not to chat with it in a terminal for sport. It is to take a messy browser conversation, drop it into a vault, and get a short note back — on this machine, with no cloud in the middle.

That needs three pieces. Ollama serves the model. Obsidian holds the Markdown. The Obsidian Web Clipper in Firefox is the missing hose: it is what turns a Grok or Gemini thread into a file the model can read. Ollama never sees the “active note”. It sees text.

A cheap ultrabook without spare RAM will crawl. If that is the box, skip local inference and use a cloud key in a later post. If the machine can keep a 7B model in memory and still leave 15–20 GB free on the NVMe, the rest of this page applies.

 

Hardware, in brief

Local inference is RAM and disk first, romance later.

  • A small 3B model is about 2 GB on disk.
  • Qwen 2.5 7B is about 4.7 GB. That is the size used below.
  • 14B and 32B models run 10–20 GB and want real headroom.

Keep 15–20 GB free before the first pull. Models accumulate.

 

Step 1: Ollama on Fedora

Install from the distro, so updates do not fight a random installer script. The weights themselves live in the home directory.

sudo dnf install ollama

sudo systemctl enable --now ollama

Library of models: ollama.com/library. Pull one and leave the daemon up:

ollama run qwen2.5:7b

Useful later:

ollama list

systemctl status ollama

The API is http://localhost:11434. Opening that URL in Firefox only answers “the service is alive”. Prompts do not go there.

 

Step 2: Obsidian (Flatpak)
flatpak install flathub md.obsidian.Obsidian

Give the sandbox write access to the vault folder. Community plugin: Text Generator (or any local-LLM plugin). Provider URL http://localhost:11434. Model name exactly as in ollama list.

Commands for the model belong in Obsidian: Ctrl+P, then the Text Generator command, with the note open. The Konsole ollama run line is optional, for talking to the model outside the vault.

 

Step 3: Firefox Web Clipper

Add-on: Obsidian Web Clipper.

Set the vault name to the name Obsidian shows, not the filesystem path. Send clips to an Inbox/ folder. The template must contain {{content}}. A template that only has {{title}} produces an empty note.

On Fedora, Firefox, and Obsidian as Flatpak, the clipper often writes the title and nothing else. Two settings fix most of that:

  • Clipper → General → Legacy mode on.
  • If a clip still arrives empty, quit Obsidian completely and clip again.

Fedora 45 Beta KDE was kinder than older spins, but legacy mode remains the reliable switch. Without it, the obsidian:// hand-off on Wayland/Flatpak drops the body.

 

What a chat page is (and is not)

Grok and Gemini are web apps, not articles. Only the turns currently mounted in the page exist in the DOM. Ctrl+A and the clipper both see that window, not the whole history.

For a long thread:

  1. Scroll to the start, wait, scroll back down so older turns load.
  2. Clip or copy in two or three chunks into the same Inbox note.
  3. Do not expect one click to swallow a fifty-turn conversation. Linux also truncates a very large obsidian:// payload — that is why legacy mode still stops after a handful of exchanges on a long Grok chat.

Short page or short chat: clipper in legacy mode. Long Grok/Gemini thread: scroll, piece it, then the model.

You must be signed in. A logged-out Grok page clips the login screen.

 

Step 4: Let Ollama tidy the file

With the raw .md open, run Text Generator. Put the instruction after the pasted dialogue. If the plugin only receives the instruction, the 7B model writes a tutorial instead of a note.

Turn the dialogue above into a vault note.
Headings: Done / Decisions / Open.
European Portuguese or English — match the dialogue.
No how-to. No jokes. If it is not in the dialogue, omit it.

A system line in the plugin helps: “You are a clerk. You output Markdown. You never explain how to work.”

Two Inbox notes become one by pasting both under headings in a third note, then generating once. Or, from Konsole:

cat "/path/to/vault/Inbox/a.md" "/path/to/vault/Inbox/b.md" \
  | ollama run qwen2.5:7b "Vault note. Done / Decisions / Open. No tutorial."

A 7B model will ramble if you feed it a clipped mess and a soft prompt. Shorter chunks, then merge the three Done lists by hand, beat one giant run.

 

The pipeline, once

Firefox (Web Clipper, legacy mode) → Inbox/*.md → Text Generator + Ollama → a short note in Chats/.

The add-on captures. The model cleans. Neither step replaces the other.

 

What’s next

If the machine cannot host a 7B model at a usable speed, the follow-up is Google AI Studio as the provider inside the same Obsidian plugin — same vault, no local weights.
entry.summary: Run Ollama on Fedora, clip browser chats into an Obsidian vault, and tidy them with a local model. What actually works with Firefox and Flatpak.

entry.title: Installing Fedora 45 Beta KDE Plasma
entry.content:
Get Fedora 45 Beta KDE Plasma

Use Fedora Media Writer application to create a ‘Live USB’.

Fedora Media Writer is available for Linux, Microsoft Windows and Mac.

 

Install Fedora

Fedora images are hybrid ISO images, so they can be used for DVD burning or flash drive creation. They also work on BIOS and UEFI systems.

As this is a “live” distribution, the new OS (operating system) will run from the DVD or pen drive without making any changes to the hard disk. You can test the OS and only then install it on the hard drive.

During installation, create a user and set the password.

After installation, restart the computer and remove the DVD or flash drive. Log in, open Terminal and update the entire system with the following command:

sudo dnf update

(enter password)

Restart the computer to load a new kernel and start the updated applications. Restart on the desktop or with the reboot command.

reboot

 

Parameterize DNF

Fedora uses DNF to install and update its software over the internet. It also automatically determines application dependencies.

Repositories Fedora
Fedora includes two repositories by default: fedora, with the same software packages as the DVD and updates, with updated packages. These repositories sign their RPM files to make sure they are valid when they are downloaded.

Other Repositories
For applications that conflict with Fedora policy (MP3, DVD, MPEG, binary drivers, etc.) the RPM Fusion repository is required.

sudo dnf install https://download1.rpmfusion.org/free/fedora/rpmfusion-free-release-$(rpm -E %fedora).noarch.rpm https://download1.rpmfusion.org/nonfree/fedora/rpmfusion-nonfree-release-$(rpm -E %fedora).noarch.rpm

 

Install codecs

Switch to full ffmpeg

sudo dnf swap ffmpeg-free ffmpeg --allowerasing

Install additional codecs

sudo dnf update @multimedia --setopt="install_weak_deps=False" --exclude=PackageKit-gstreamer-plugin

Install the hardware accelerated codec for an Intel recent CPU…

sudo dnf install intel-media-driver

… or for an older Intel CPU.

sudo dnf install libva-intel-driver

In case it is AMD hardware (mesa):

sudo dnf install mesa-va-drivers-freeworld

To play a DVD you need to install the libdvdcss package

sudo dnf install rpmfusion-free-release-tainted

sudo dnf install libdvdcss

sudo dnf install rpmfusion-nonfree-release-tainted

sudo dnf --repo=rpmfusion-nonfree-tainted install "*-firmware"

 

Install current applications
dnf install install thunderbird ktorrent gimp gimp-help gimp-help-pt_BR unrar gsmartcontrol libreoffice-langpack-pt-PT haruna amarok inkscape kde-l10n-pt kate kdenlive krita xsane

 

Installing KDevelop IDE (for developers)
sudo dnf group install development-tools

sudo dnf group install c-development

sudo dnf install kdevelop kdevelop-pg-qt kdevelop-php

entry.title: Logitech MX Master 4 on Fedora Linux – My Final Solaar Configuration

link.title: Logitech MX Master 4 on Fedora Linux – My Final Solaar Configuration

entry.content:
The MX Master 4 is a fantastic productivity mouse, but its advanced features (custom buttons, horizontal scroll with the thumb wheel, SmartShift, Action Ring, etc.) are not fully supported out of the box on Fedora with Wayland.

Solaar is the best open-source tool for configuring Logitech devices on Linux. It allows us to customize buttons, create rules, and unlock most of the mouse’s potential.

After many hours of testing and tweaking, here is my stable daily configuration.

 

1. Installing Solaar
sudo dnf install solaar

 

2. udev Rule (Recommended)

This rule improves stability and permissions for custom rules on Wayland:

sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/44-logitech-unify-permissions.rules << 'EOF'
# Solaar - Logitech MX Master 4
KERNEL=="uinput", SUBSYSTEM=="misc", TAG+="uaccess", OPTIONS+="static_node=uinput"

ACTION=="remove", GOTO="solaar_end"
SUBSYSTEM!="hidraw", GOTO="solaar_end"

# USB-connected Logitech receivers
ATTRS{idVendor}=="046d", GOTO="solaar_apply"

# Bluetooth-connected Logitech devices (MX Master 4)
KERNELS=="0005:046D:*", GOTO="solaar_apply"

GOTO="solaar_end"

LABEL="solaar_apply"
TAG+="uaccess"

LABEL="solaar_end"
EOF

Apply the rules:

sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger

Recommendation: Reboot your system after creating this file.

 

3. Solaar GUI Settings

Open Solaar, select your MX Master 4 on the left side, and configure the following:

Parameter Recommended Value Notes
Scroll Wheel Direction Off -
Scroll Wheel Resolution Off -
Scroll Wheel Diversion Off -
Scroll Wheel Ratchet Torque 90 Feel of the clicks
Scroll Wheel Ratcheted Ratcheted Click mode by default
Scroll Wheel Ratchet Speed 18 Responsiveness
Thumb Wheel Direction Off -
Thumb Wheel Diversion On Important for horizontal scroll
Sensibilidade (DPI) 1600 Comfortable speed
Haptic Feedback Level 35 Not too strong

 

4. Final Button Configuration
Physical Button Key/Button Actions Key/Button Diversion Reason
Middle Button Mouse Middle Button Regular Open links in new tab
Back Button Mouse Back Button Regular Go back
Forward Button Mouse Forward Button Regular Navigate forward
Gestures Gesture Button Diverted Paste (Ctrl + V)
Haptic (Large Thumb Button) unknown:0199 Diverted Fast copy (Ctrl + C)
Shift wheel mode Smart Shift Regular -
       

Tip: Leave the small button behind the scroll wheel as SmartShift (toggles Ratcheted / Free Spin).

The Thumb Wheel (horizontal scroll) is configured via a custom rule in the rules.yaml file.

 

5. Custom Rules (rules.yaml)

The custom rules are stored in:

~/.config/solaar/rules.yaml

First, make a backup of the current file (if it exists).

cp ~/.config/solaar/rules.yaml ~/.config/solaar/rules.yaml.backup 2>/dev/null || true

Create the new rules file

cat > ~/.config/solaar/rules.yaml << 'EOF'
%YAML 1.3
---
- Key: [Haptic, pressed]
  KeyPress:
    - [Control_L, c]
    - click
...
---
- Key: [Mouse Gesture Button, pressed]
  KeyPress:
    - [Control_L, v]
    - click
...
---
- Rule:
    - Test: thumb_wheel_up
    - MouseScroll: [2, 0]
- Rule:
    - Test: thumb_wheel_down
    - MouseScroll: [-2, 0]
...
EOF

After creating the file, restart Solaar or log out and back in.

Note: You can adjust scroll speed by changing the values 2 and -2. Only integers are accepted (e.g. [3, 0] and [-3, 0] for faster scrolling).

 

Tip: Always keep a backup of your rules.yaml before doing a clean Fedora upgrade.

entry.title: How to Backup and Restore Thunderbird Remote Images Whitelist (Clean Install)

link.title: How to Backup and Restore Thunderbird Remote Images Whitelist (Clean Install)

entry.content:
Every time I do a clean installation of Thunderbird, I have to manually reconfigure the whitelist for loading remote images from trusted senders. This guide shows a quick and clean way to backup and restore that setting without carrying over unnecessary profile data.

Note: This method is specific to Fedora Linux (and other Linux distributions using the same folder structure). It does not apply to Windows or macOS.

Backup (on your current Thunderbird)

Close Thunderbird completely.

Open a terminal and run:

cp ~/.thunderbird/*.default-esr/permissions.sqlite ~/permissions.sqlite

The file permissions.sqlite will be saved in your Home folder. Copy it to a safe place (USB drive, external disk, etc.).

Restore (on a new Thunderbird installation)
  1. Install Thunderbird and open it once (it will create the new profile).
  2. Close Thunderbird.
  3. Open your file manager and go to your Home folder.
  4. Press Ctrl + H to show hidden files.
  5. Enter the folder .thunderbird.
  6. Open the folder that ends with .default-esr.
  7. Rename the existing permissions.sqlite file to permissions-old.sqlite (just in case).
  8. Copy your backup file permissions.sqlite into this folder (replace when asked).
  9. Open Thunderbird again.

Your remote images whitelist will be restored.

entry.title: Installing Fedora 44 Xfce
entry.content:

As this is a “live” distribution, the new OS (operating system) will run from the pen drive without making any changes to the hard disk. You can test the OS and only then install it on the hard drive.

During installation, create a user, set the password and leave the “root” account disabled.

After installation, restart the computer and remove the DVD or flash drive. Log in, open Terminal and update the entire system with the following command:

sudo dnf update

(enter password)

Restart the computer to load a new kernel and start the updated applications. Restart on the desktop or with the reboot command.

reboot

Install codecs

Switch to full ffmpeg

sudo dnf swap ffmpeg-free ffmpeg --allowerasing

Install additional codecs

sudo dnf update @multimedia --setopt="install_weak_deps=False" --exclude=PackageKit-gstreamer-plugin

Install the hardware accelerated codec for an Intel recent CPU…

sudo dnf install intel-media-driver

… or for an older Intel CPU.

sudo dnf install libva-intel-driver

In case it is AMD hardware (mesa):

sudo dnf install mesa-va-drivers-freeworld

To play a DVD you need to install the libdvdcss package

sudo dnf install rpmfusion-free-release-tainted

sudo dnf install libdvdcss

sudo dnf install rpmfusion-nonfree-release-tainted

sudo dnf --repo=rpmfusion-nonfree-tainted install "*-firmware"

 

Install current applications
sudo dnf install thunderbird 7zip unrar gsmartcontrol libreoffice-draw libreoffice-impress libreoffice-langpack-pt-PT vlc geeqie hplip-gui simple-scan

 

Remove redundant applications
sudo dnf remove claws-mail geany

 

Automatic login (optional)

Edit /etc/lightdm/lightdm.conf –> autologin-user = username

sudo nano /etc/lightdm/lightdm.conf

 

How to change the hostname

If you want to customize the machine name, the easiest method is using the command line.

This instruction is valid for a computer used at home, which is not part of a enterprise network. We use the hostnamectl command:

hostnamectl set-hostname new-name

This name is stored in the /etc/hostname file.

We can simultaneously check the machine name, operating system, kernel version and architecture with this command:

hostnamectl status

sudo dnf install rpmfusion-nonfree-release-tainted

sudo dnf --repo=rpmfusion-nonfree-tainted install "*-firmware"

 

Installing KDevelop IDE (for developers)

entry.title: XPPen Driver Install on Fedora 42+
entry.content:
The XP-Pen Artist 12 3rd Gen is a compact, portable 11.9-inch drawing display launched in late 2025, offering excellent value for beginner to intermediate digital artists. Featuring a Full HD laminated screen with anti-glare etched glass (99% sRGB coverage), it delivers vibrant colors and a natural paper-like texture. The battery-free X4 stylus provides 16,384 levels of pressure, 60° tilt support, and ultra-low 2g activation force for smooth, precise strokes. It includes eight customizable express keys and two innovative X-Dials for quick access to zoom, brush size, and other shortcuts. With a single USB-C cable for video, data, and power, plus broad compatibility (Linux, Windows, macOS, Android), this lightweight (~719g) tablet is an affordable yet feature-rich choice for on-the-go creativity.

In recent months it has no longer been possible to install the drawing display driver via “Discover”. Through the “Terminal” we get the following error: “package does not verify: no digest”. Several attempts with the “dnf install” command also fail.

Searching for the error in the file, the result is:

pratajo@amd64:~$ rpm -K XPPenLinux-xxxx.rpm
XPPenLinux-xxxx.rpm: DIGESTS NOT-OK

Grok explains that this is quite common in recent Fedora versions (especially Fedora 42/43+ in 2026), because RPM has been updated to more modern versions (RPM 6.0+ or equivalents) that reject packages without strong digests (such as SHA-256) or that use obsolete algorithms (old MD5/SHA-1). Many third-party or older packages haven’t been rebuilt/updated for this yet, which is why you need to bypass the check with –nodigest.

The solution I found was to install the rpm directly, using a command with flags to bypass the checks:

sudo rpm -Uvh --nodigest --nosignature ./XPPenLinux-xxxx.rpm
